title: Choose a homepage composition
question: Which first-screen structure should carry Radiance’s story? Each keeps the current dark-violet identity, editorial serif, truthful Personal Intelligence details, and a direct path to the real chat.

options.label: The Working Proof
options.thesis: An editor’s proof sheet connects a note you chose to the shape of a later answer.
options.viewport: One broad proof sheet holds the promise, a working Chat action, and a continuous note-to-question-to-reply example.
options.risk: The proof-sheet form could feel like publishing software unless the real chat action stays prominent.

options.label: The Annotated Edition
options.thesis: A reader’s edition places a later question beside the notes and answer preferences that inform it.
options.viewport: An oversized promise opens into a readable conversation passage, with the selected context in a functional outer margin and the Chat action above the fold.
options.risk: The literary form may make Radiance feel like a reading product rather than an AI workspace.

options.label: The Personal Index
options.thesis: A reference index makes saved context, answer preferences, and sharing control easy to scan.
options.viewport: A clear typographic index leads into one featured note and a later question, with the primary Chat action embedded in the page masthead.
options.risk: An index can read like Settings and underplay the conversational outcome.
